page: Amazon Web Services m9g.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 virtual-CPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The configuration includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no local instance storage.

Benchmark testing displays exceptional single-threaded performance and memory throughput. The instance ranks in the top tier for Geekbench single-core performance (2,334.0), PassMark memory evaluation (4,552.85), gzip compression (36.42 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (17.14 GB/sec). Multi-core benchmarks also demonstrate high capability, with Geekbench multi-core hitting 19,581.0 and static web serving throughput achieving 54.3 GB/sec. Small language model token generation is similarly strong, producing 376.71 tokens per second on a 135M model and 30.2 tokens per second on a 7B model. Conversely, integer stress testing and Redis operations settle within median industry percentiles.

The physical-core layout without simultaneous multithreading delivers consistent compute performance and prevents thread contention under sustained workloads. However, the absence of bundled local NVMe storage means the instance relies entirely on external EBS block storage for persistent or scratch volumes, and the lack of discrete GPUs limits its application for massive matrix calculations. The m9g.4xlarge offers high computational density and memory efficiency per core for general-purpose workloads, microservice hosting, static web routing, data transformation pipelines, and relational or document database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro system and ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores at 3.3 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, 64.0 GB of system memory, an 8 Gbps baseline network interface, and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the m9g.4xlarge demonstrates top-tier single-core Geekbench scores, excellent memory subsystem ratings, and rapid compression throughput. Multi-core operations remain solid across static web delivery and small-to-medium language model text generation. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete reliance on network-attached storage for disk operations. This instance delivers balanced resource allocation and high operational efficiency for web backends, caching services, software builds, and transactional databases.
